- Our APAC office also needs to know VAT handling on the invoice — do you issue a credit-note or VAT refund if fees are deducted by banks and reduce the amount actually received?

We've attached the remittance file we attempted to send and the returned SWIFT notice. Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Daniel

Hi Daniel — thanks for the quick note and the SWIFT return. I pulled finance and legal into this thread and attached our standard bank instructions (Bank_Instructions_NOSTRO.pdf). High level:

- Preferred: send the gross USD amount to our Nostro account (account credited at Redwood), including a clear SWIFT field for the intermediary so the beneficiary receives the full invoice value. Our bank details are in the attached PDF (Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Inc., Bank: First Global Bank, Account: 0123456789, SWIFT: FGBBUS33).
- If your bank MUST deduct correspondent fees (common in some APAC corridors), please notify us before sending. We can either: (a) accept net receipts and issue a shortfall credit note for VAT reconciliation, or (b) ask you to top-up for the shortfall so the net received equals the invoice.
- VAT: for APAC customers we typically do not separately reclaim VAT for bank fee shortfalls — VAT is calculated on the billed amount. If the received amount is lower because of bank fees, we can issue a credit note to BrightShip to correct VAT reporting, provided you confirm the fee amounts and provide the intermediary fee stub.

Given this is time-sensitive, if you can share the returned SWIFT as text (or your bank's intermediary routing), we can flag the exact correspondent to your bank to avoid the route that strips the fields.

I've cc'd Marissa (sales lead on this account) and Rishi (finance ops) so they can confirm whether Redwood will make a one-time exception on fee absorption in this billing cycle.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
